With \(\vec a=\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k,\ \vec b=\hat i-\hat j,\ \vec c=\hat i-\hat j-\hat k\): \[\vec r = (1+\lambda)\hat i + (-1+2\lambda)\hat j + (-1-\lambda)\hat k.\] Impose \(\vec r\cdot\vec b = 0\): \((1+\lambda) - (-1+2\lambda) = 2 - \lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 2.\) Then \[\vec r\cdot\vec a = \vec c\cdot\vec a + \lambda\,|\vec a|^2.\] Now \(\vec c\cdot\vec a = 1-2+1 = 0\) and \(|\vec a|^2 = 1+4+1 = 6\), so \(\vec r\cdot\vec a = 0 + 2(6) = 12.\)
authoredSolutions.89: The condition \(A^2 = I_3\) with \(A\) symmetric means the rows are orthonormal. Diagonal entries of \(A^2\) give \(x^2+y^2+z^2 = 1\); off-diagonal entries give \(xy+yz+zx = 0\). Hence \[(x+y+z)^2 = (x^2+y^2+z^2) + 2(xy+yz+zx) = 1 + 0 = 1,\] and since \(x+y+z>0\), \(x+y+z = 1\). Using \[x^3+y^3+z^3 - 3xyz = (x+y+z)\big(x^2+y^2+z^2 - xy-yz-zx\big) = 1\cdot(1-0) = 1,\] we get \(x^3+y^3+z^3 = 1 + 3xyz = 1 + 3(2) = 7.\)
authoredSolutions.90: We form \(3\)-digit numbers (between \(100\) and \(1000\)) from \(\{1,2,3,4,5\}\) without repetition, divisible by \(3\) or \(5\). Divisible by \(3\): choose \(3\) digits with sum a multiple of \(3\): \(\{1,2,3\},\{1,3,5\},\{2,3,4\},\{3,4,5\}\) — \(4\) sets, each \(3! = 6\) arrangements, so \(24\). Divisible by \(5\): last digit \(5\), first two from remaining \(4\): \(4\times 3 = 12\). Divisible by both (i.e. by \(15\)): sum-of-\(3\) divisible by \(3\) and ending in \(5\): sets \(\{1,3,5\},\{3,4,5\}\), each with \(5\) fixed last and \(2! = 2\) arrangements, so \(2\times 2 = 4\). By inclusion–exclusion: \[24 + 12 - 4 = 32.\]
